key_insight: V-PaSS improves prediction for unfamiliar perovskite solar cells by representing alloy continuity and device physics rather than treating materials as arbitrary labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber alloys and device stacks with better transfer to materials and laboratories absent from training.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, n-i-p or p-i-n polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Use a scientific language model to encode chemical descriptions.
evidence_signal: On institution-grouped evaluation with unseen test laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Endpoint interpolation assumes solid-solution continuity; the abstract does not establish reliability for alloys with phase changes or structures outside that assumption.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
